Specification Talk Structured

A workflow proposed to use language models (LLMs, AI systems that generate text) in the discovery and registration of requirements, with decisions made by people with authority and traceable divergences between documentation, testing and code.

Proposal Developmental framework. The complete workflow has not yet been compared to a baseline; components have partial evidence.

The Problem Summary

Generating faster code does not in itself preserve business intent

AI agents interpret instructions, consult files, propose changes, generate Code and run tests. This reduces the effort to implement, but does not guarantee that the The solution corresponds to the problem that should be solved.

When the agent binds tasks, an incomplete interpretation crosses several Artifacts before anyone could see it. The risk is not just the wrong code: it is a interpretation not yet validated to become an apparently consistent implementation. In legacy systems (old systems that follow in production), business is spread between code, integrations, outdated documentation and the memory of few people.

Not even the speed gain is consensus. In a controlled task, developers with AI finished faster (Peng et al., 2023). In a study with 16 developers experienced and 246 real tasks, the use of AI increased time by 19% (Becker et al., 2025, preprint, still no peer review). The page does not discuss how much faster If it comes, it's what's lost on the way.

The same failure, seen when it reaches production in a system that seems to work: The Silent Crash. Base: Hou et al. (2024), systematic review of the use of LLMs in software engineering, which attests to the wide use, not the effectiveness of this workflow.

The Cause illustrative scenario

A request for modernization mixes four different things

The scenario, built for this page, is the modernization of a commercial system with over 15 years: proposals, commercial conditions, approvals, contracts and integration With the billing. Changes take weeks, and few people know all rules. The board asks:

“ We need to modernise this system by migrating to a more current architecture(supposed solution), without interrupting the operation(objective) and without losing existing business rules(objective).”

The phrase expresses a legitimate intention, but it does not say what to preserve, what to change or how to measure success. It gathers symptoms, needs to investigate, goals and a solution already chosen, and each category requires a different treatment.

Figure 3 · Order noted. The literal phrase contains only objectives and a solution; the need does not appear in it.
CategoryIn the scenarioTreatment
Symptomslengthy changes, recurrent incidents, dependence on expertsinvestigate the cause
Needs to investigatereduce cost and risk of changes; depend less on tacit knowledge (what people know and never wrote)confirm with evidence
Declared objectives“without interrupting the operation”, “without losing the rules”make verifiable (what rules?)
Presupposed solution“most current architecture”evaluate as an alternative, not as a requirement

There is a second cause, decisive in legacy: the current behavior of the system does not It's necessarily the desired behavior. A rule can be preserved, corrected, replaced or discontinued, and the decision depends on evidence and Business authority, not what the code executes today.

The request then becomes a sequence of decisions. At each stage there is one point where the AI help and another in which it can distort, mapped into Step by step.

See also: formulate the problem before compromising the solution and the same survey of the current state (As-Is), applied the legacy Salesforce. Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 (request, analyse, specify, validate and manage requirements; verification and validation are different things); NASA Systems Engineering Handbook (needs) respond to the problem without prescribing solution; Ferrari et al. (2016) and Burnay et al. (2014) (ambiguities reveal tacit knowledge; stakeholders omit topics that no one else question), reasons to talk with operation, support and integrations, and not just read the code.

The proposed solution Proposal

AI expands research; people with authority decide

Structured Conversational Specification is a human–IA workflow, governed by artifacts and by human authority, to elicit, record, test and evolve to the intention of a system as verifiable requirements and criteria, keeping explicit the sources, uncertainties, decisions and form of verification.

The model can ask, summarize, propose scenarios, point contradictions, recover context and prepare changes. By default, you don't get the authority to decide value, risk, compliance, acceptance or truth of domain. The position is compatible with elicitation, analysis, validation and management activities described in ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and in SWEBOK (the IEEE Computer Software Engineering Knowledge Guide) Society); the proposal explores how the AI can support them without replacing them.

Spec-first

Purpose: align the intention before the code.

Risk: early freeze a model interpretation.

Spec-retrospective

Purpose: reconstruct the intention from code, logs and incidents.

Risk: give consistency to what was accidental.

In legacy, both modes appear.

The strongest objection: is this requirements engineering with another name?

Mostly, yeah. The possible contribution is interface and orchestration, and only exists if the workflow specifies entries, revision gates, artifact types, authority, provenance (the record of origin and of whom it decided), divergence and metrics. Talking to AI and going out with a Markdown file is not that.

What's not

  • Validated method or standard.
  • Replacement of requirements engineering, architecture, security or governance.
  • Business validation for chat approval.
  • Guarantee of completeness, absence of hallucination or end of divergence between artifacts.
  • TDD, BDD or Example Mapping with another name.

Terminology note

This framework has already been called Vibe Spec-ing. The name changed because “live” suggests the opposite of what the proposal requires: registration, authority and verification. Similar labels (vibe specs, vibe speccing) circulate informally for AI interviews before code or for generated specifications Of agents' logs.

Related practice: Vibe Coding with Devin, orchestration of staff complementing this proposal; and Agent-driven governance. Base: SWEBOK Guide v4.0a (Requirement Area) and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 as reference Discipline; Böckeler/Thoughtworks (2025) on “spec-drive development” as a label still unstable (spec-first, spec-anchored, spec-as-source). The informal use of the label (marmelab, 2025; Bechtel; McGuinness) is cited as use, not as evidence.

The whole workflow Proposal

Step by step: what AI accelerates and what it can distort

Those who know Design Thinking recognize four of the five stages. The fifth, specify and evolve the artifacts, is the addition of requirements engineering. At each stage the Win comes along with a known risk and a control. It's a cycle, not a sequence: any step returns to the previous when new evidence arises. The Vocabulary of Design Thinking serves as a map; it is not presented as proof of anything.

Figure 5 · Map of steps: gain, risk and control
StepWhere the AI helpsWhat can distortControlSection
Discover suggest questions and point out topics that no one mentioned abstract that deforms reports; synthetic personas (users simulated by AI) can anchor stereotypes; illusion of completeness record source; check with operation observation and legacy inspection Protocol
Set problem can help separate symptom, need, objective and presumed solution chance of result becoming requirement; early frozen solution human decision before formalizing; validating understanding is not validating the result Cause
Explore Examples generate normal, limit and negative cases fluent specification that hides false premise; harmonised conflict in silence examples validated by those who know the domain; conflict preserved, not solved by the model Protocol
Specify and evolve structure the specification and propose traceability links drift (the specification and code move away without anyone noticing); loss of who decided, with what evidence and what was rejected divergence policy; provenance; traceability (the link between decision, rule, test and code); history that does not erase versions Divergence
Test and validate translate criteria into tests and support characterization tests green test against an oracle (the expected result) wrong, written by the AI itself oracle defined by persons; independent tests TDD

Protocol Proposal illustrative scenario

Five practices for AI exit to be challenged

The contribution of the model is only useful when your outputs can be examined and contested. Start with a representative flow, not the entire system. On the set, the approval of a proposal with exceptional discount.

  1. Record the origin of each statement.

    Interview, document, code inspection, operational observation, inference or formal decision. The conversation with the model does not replace observing the operation or inspecting the legacy: the sources confer on each other.

  2. Separate facts, hypotheses and proposals.

    A plausible response from the model is not evidence that the rule exists.

  3. Keep to-dos visible.

    Relevant uncertainty remains open, responsible, until it is resolved or accepted as a risk.

  4. Use examples and counterexamples.

    Normal situation, limit and exception. In the scenario: within the limit, automatic approval; above, authorized person and justification; incomplete data, the proposal does not advance; altered value after approval, may require further evaluation. They're hypotheses until confirmation. The model suggests cases; it does not promote the approved rule.

  5. Risk proportional review.

    Commercial, regulatory and critical integration decisions go through those with authority.

It is not bureaucracy for every sentence: it is to be able to distinguish what is known, what is supposed to be and what you've decided. And validating understanding is not validating the result. The conversation shows if people understand the rule in the same way, not that modernization goes reduce incidents.

See also: Reveal Implicit to Make It Explicit (inventory of the current state and separation between fact, inference and judgment), when you stop investigating and typed and addressable knowledge. Base: the NIST generating AI profile (AI 600-1) treats confabulation (responses plausible and false) and human configuration–IA as risks to manage; W3C PROV-DM offers a model to register provenance (entity, activity, agent); Parasuraman & Manzey (2010) and Buçinca et al. (2021) on automation bias, with functions of cognitive strength that reduced excessive dependence on AI in an experiment; Cucumber, Example Mapping (rules, examples and questions); SWEBOK lists various sources of requirements (interested parties, business rules, domain knowledge, environment operational), triangulation basis in practice 1.

Governance Proposal

Who decides what, and what the AI can do in every decision

The matrix separates assistance authority. It is a proposed governance policy, the adjust to the structure of responsibility of each organization, and not a requirement of standard.

When the agent also executes tools, changes files or triggers pipelines, the controls begin to cover permissions, scope of execution, revision of changes and Break conditions: generate a suggestion and perform an action are different levels autonomy. The oracle line connects this section to TDD: the AI may write the test code, but the expected result comes from those who have authority over The rule.

Divergence Proposal illustrative scenario

No artifact alone preserves intent

Documentation, testing and code will diverge. What matters is who solves, how, and where The decision is registered.

Each artifact has a responsibility and a limit. Business rules register adopted policies, but do not guarantee implementation. The characterization tests record the legacy, including defects and obsolete rules. The code implements a version, but does not prove adherence to intent. There is no universal source of truth.

The divergence (in English, drift) is the situation in which artifacts should Saying the same thing starts to say different things. The proposed policy has five steps, shown below in the discount example.

The reverse: if the new code does not meet an approved criterion, change the criterion requires explicit decision. Editing the test for him to pass is a decision without registration. A traceability is valid in both directions (decision → criterion → test → component; failure → rule to review), with depth proportional to criticality and the requirement of audit. The goal is not to prevent all divergence, but to make it detectable, Explicable and treatable.

Specification and TDD Summary Evidence

The specification decides what to check; the TDD checks

A term before following: oracle is the source of the expected result with that the test compares the observed behavior.

The difference between approaches is the control unit. The TDD (write a test that failure, minimum code for it to pass, and then refactor) answers “what’s next smaller increment and how do I find that it continues to work?”. The specification answers “what problem, for whom, with what rules, restrictions and criteria?”. The TDD makes feedback cheap; does not make the oracle correct. Without intention and scope, TDD can test the wrong thing efficiently. Without executable oracles, the specification can document a wrong intention.

There is a specific risk of agents: when the same model writes the specification and tests, a green test can only confirm the error of the model itself. Control is the expected result is defined or validated by people before the test is generated (the oracle line in Who decides what?), and each criterion critical have at least one test that was not born from the same prompt or from the same context.

In legacy, three types of tests have different roles: characterization (what legacy today), acceptance (the approved criteria) and TDD (local implementation). One possible sequence: characterize the legacy, validate the rules with whom it decides, write acceptance tests, implement with TDD, compare results and release with monitoring, interruption and reversal criteria.

Specification × TDD, criterion by criterion
CriteriaConversational specificationTDD
PurposeReduce loss of intent between conversation, requirements, code and testingGuide incremental design and implementation by executable tests with quick feedback
Control unitProduct intent, rules, restrictions and criteriaObservable code behaviour, in general function, class or module
OracleIt is only verifiable if each requirement has observable condition, limits and procedure; fluent text or human approval is not enoughA green test only ensures that the exercised behavior satisfies the oracle encoded in that environment
DivergenceHigh risk of drift spec; requires explicit policy, versioning and detectionDetects regression in what is exercised; tests can become obsolete or be changed to accommodate code
EvidenceComponents with isolated studies; complete workflow without localized studySmall and contextual effect (see below)

The evidence about the TDD is greater than that of this workflow, and contextual. Rafique & Mišić (2013), in a meta-analysis of 27 studies, found small effect on quality and little or no in productivity. Tosun et al. (2017), with 24 professionals, no found statistical difference in external quality and saw a drop in productivity in the complex task in existing code. Nagappan et al. (2008), in four IBM teams and Microsoft, observed defects density 40–90% lower and 15–35% longer development, with threats to validity declared by the authors. Liu et al. (2023), EvalPlus) showed that expanded tests find errors that the original tests Let them through. The conclusion is that the proposal does not claim superiority over the TDD nor replaces it: provides context and decisions; TDD provides local feedback and protection against regression.

See also: the failure that 54 tests did not catch, Passing the test isn't the same as being right, from spec to Apex Test in Salesforce practice, the same logic in accessibility and from legacy (As-Is) to target (To-Be). Base: Beck (2002), TDD; Feathers (2004), legacy code characterization tests.

Measure and Limits Not validated Evidence

What to measure, and what this proposal still does not prove

Modernisation is not complete because the code has been rewritten. Indicators below need operational definition, baseline and observation period; more documents or tests do not prove, alone, that the system has become more sustainable. As complete definitions (recall of requirements, residual ambiguity per 100 requirements, precision and recall of links, DORA metrics) are in the kit.

Case

  • Critical rules identified and validated.
  • Criteria covered by at least one independent test (not generated from the same specification prompt).
  • Divergences between specification, testing and production by release, by gravity.
  • Statements and decisions with complete provenance: source, author, date and justification.
  • Time to rebuild the justification for an old decision.

Operational output

  • Time to understand and implement a rule change.
  • Incidents, regressions and emergency corrections after release.
  • Rework attributed to the divergence between intention and implementation, measurable because the divergence policy classifies the cause.

Evidence ladder

Climbing a step requires new evidence; the bottom step does not prove the top step.

  1. 1. Agent capacity Studyed on isolated tasks
  2. 2. Artifact quality Studyed on isolated tasks
  3. 3. Task result No full workflow study
  4. 4. Operational output No full workflow study
  5. 5. Business result No full workflow study

What Literature Lets You Say Today

LLMs show partial capacity in controlled bidding tasks, generation of specification and detection of ambiguity, with flaws in domain terminology, interfaces and restrictions. The research is mostly laboratory, and LLMs as requirements reviewers had inconsistent results. No study was found controlled or longitudinal workflow complete against a baseline aligned to ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and SWEBOK.

How to evaluate in your context

  1. Set up an independent reference package

    Needs, rules, restrictions and border cases, before or in parallel to solicitation.

  2. Conduct IA-elication by registering source

    Separating fact, inference and proposition.

  3. Blind Review

    By at least two people in the domain.

  4. Measure in four points

    After the definition, specification, implementation and operation.

  5. Post prompts, model versions, artifacts and award decisions

    Respecting privacy.

  6. Treat any improvement as local evidence

    Not as general workflow validation.

The comparison with a human or hybrid baseline and the H1–H4 hypotheses are in the kit.

See also: how to refute a hypothesis, what an article does not yet prove, limits in the case of accessibility, support (incidents and emergency corrections as indicator) and the total cost of the AI, including inference and review. Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15939:2017 (measurement part of a need for information with baseline), ISO/IEC 25010:2023 (product quality attributes) and DORA (delivery time, failure rate of change, recovery) serve as a reference to define indicators. Studies: Ronanki et al. (2023), Krishna et al. (2024), Bashir et al. (2025), Zadenoori et al. (2025, preprint), Norheim et al. (2024), Seifert et al., Montgomery et al. (2022).

Where to start

Start with a flow, not the entire system.

Choose a representative flow, apply the five practices, register the first divergence and decide who solves it. No promise of outcome: the goal is to have something which may be examined and contested.

In short

What is Structured Conversational Specification

It's a workflow proposal where the AI helps to elicit and register requirements — asking, comparing interpretations and suggesting examples — while persons with authority decide. Each statement has origin and status, and differences between documentation, testing and code follow an explicit policy. The efficacy of complete workflow has not yet been evaluated.

  • The IA proposes, people decide — the authority matrix separates those who decide who attends; the model has no substantive authority by default.
  • Five Practices — record the origin, separate fact of hypothesis, keep to-dos visible, use examples and counterexamples, and review in proportion to the risk.
  • Governmentd Divergence — documentation, testing and code will diverge; policy defines who resolves, how, and where the decision is registered.
  • Complements TDD, does not replace it — the specification decides what to verify; the TDD checks. The oracle (expected result) comes from people.

Part of the same method of Trust Engineering and practice of Vibe Coding with Devin: the registered intention, with human authority, before the code.

Frequently Asked Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Structured Conversational Specification?

It is a human workflow–IA, governed by artifacts and by human authority, to elicit, record, test and evolve the intention of a system as verifiable requirements and criteria, keeping explicit the sources, uncertainties, decisions and form of verification. It is an evaluation proposal, not a validated method or a standard.

What's the difference for Vibe Spec-ing and Spec-Driven Development?

Vibe Spec-ing was the previous name of this framework; it changed because "vibe" suggests the opposite of what the proposal requires (registration, authority and verification). Spec-Driven Development is an unstable label for practices where the specification comes before the code (spec-first, spec-anchored, spec-as-source). The Structured Conversational Specification is a specific workflow within this space, with explicit human authority and policy of divergence.

Can the AI approve business requirements or rules?

No, by default. The model may ask, summarize, propose scenarios, point out contradictions and prepare changes, but does not receive authority to decide value, risk, compliance, acceptance or truth of domain. The authority matrix assigns each decision to designated persons; it is a proposed governance policy, adjusting to each organization.

Does that replace the TDD or acceptance tests?

Nope. They act at different levels: the specification defines which problem, for whom and with which criteria; the TDD verifies the next code increment. The TDD makes feedback cheap, but does not make the oracle correct. When the same model writes the specification and tests, a green test can only confirm the error of the model itself, so the expected result is defined or validated by people.

Does it work for legacy systems?

The proposal was designed for this case: characterization tests record what the legacy does today, and the decision to preserve, correct, replace or discontinue each rule is up to those who have business authority. The declared risk is post-rationalization: to give coherence to what was accidental by rebuilding the intention from the code.

Is there evidence that it works?

For isolated components, partial: studies show partial capacity of LLMs in elicitation, specification and detection of ambiguity in controlled tasks. For the complete workflow, no controlled or longitudinal study was located in front of a baseline aligned with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and SWEBOK. The page brings an evaluation protocol to test in the context itself.
